pages.quiz:
ENGLISH ACTIVITIES — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #3
====

GRADE: Grade 2
SUBJECT: ENGLISH ACTIVITIES
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Pre-reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Pre-reading.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Pre-reading.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pre-reading.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Pre-reading.

2. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. went
   B. goes
   C. going
   D. goed

3. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only an action
   B. Only a describing word
   C. A person, place, thing, or idea
   D. Only a joining word

4. When practising Pre- Writing, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Pre- Writing.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Pre- Writing.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Pre- Writing.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pre- Writing.

5. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. quickly
   B. run
   C. blue
   D. happiness

6. When practising Handwriting, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Handwriting.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Handwriting.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Handwriting.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Handwriting.

7. When practising Language structures School, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Language structures School.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Language structures School.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Language structures School.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Language structures School.

8. When practising Connected text reading and fluency, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Connected text reading and fluency.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Connected text reading and fluency.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Connected text reading and fluency.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Connected text reading and fluency.

9. When practising Pronunciation and Vocabulary, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Pronunciation and Vocabulary.

10. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. Many unrelated topics with no link
   B. No full stops
   C. One main idea with supporting sentences
   D. Only one word repeated

11. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the library?
   B. Where is the Library
   C. where is the library
   D. Where is the library

12. When practising Letter sound knowledge, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Letter sound knowledge.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Letter sound knowledge.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Letter sound knowledge.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Letter sound knowledge.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Punctuation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Guided Writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Attentive listening and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Pronunciation and Vocabulary and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pre-reading.

2. A — went

3. C — A person, place, thing, or idea

4. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pre- Writing.

5. B — run

6. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Handwriting.

7. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Language structures School.

8. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Connected text reading and fluency.

9. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pronunciation and Vocabulary.

10. C — One main idea with supporting sentences

11. A — Where is the library?

12. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Letter sound knowledge.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Punctuation; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Guided Writing; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Attentive listening; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Pronunciation and Vocabulary; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
